title: constructive solid geometry / SDF based volume algorithm
abstract: # Description I got (re-)inspired to play around with a signed distance field based raymarch algorithm by a [gamedev video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=il-TXbn5iMA) on youtube. With that you can compose various 3D shapes with operations like union, difference/subtraction, intersection, xor as well as smooth variants of the former. You can also modify shapes, e.g. by applying rounding, bending or twisting. Here's a gear as an example: ```julia sdf_tree = CSG.diff( CSG.intersect( CSG.smooth_union( CSG.Cylinder(0.2, 0.7, color = :lightgray), CSG.union( map(1:4) do n CSG.Rect( Vec3f(0.1, 0.07, 0.2), color = :lightgray, translation = 0.8 * Vec3f(cos(n * pi/8 - pi/16), sin(n * pi/8 - pi/16), 0), rotation = qrotation(Vec3f(0, 0, 1), -n * pi/8 + pi/16), ) end..., mirror = (true, true, false) ), smooth = 0.02 ), CSG.Cylinder(0.1, 1, color = :orange) ), CSG.Cylinder(0.2, 0.4), ) csgplot(-1..1, -1..1, -1..1, sdf_tree) ``` The code is currently quite messy because it contains leftovers multiple prototypes. The first is an attempt to compute signed distance fields on the GPU directly, by encoding the operations on CPU and then decoding and processing them on the GPU. I got this to work, but it was very expensive on GPU. (I'd guess this is a combination of needing a lot of branching to determine what each operation is (e.g. `if (operation == op_translation) ...`) running for multiple operations that need to be evaluated multiple times as the raymarching gets evaluated.) This is currently still available as `sdfscatter()`. The second prototype moved the SDF generation to the CPU, evaluating distances once and storing them in a 3D array. That array is then passed to `volume` where the distances are used in ray marching. On the GPU side, this is should be faster and higher quality than the other volume algorithms. The conversion for this is currently disabled. The third and current prototype builds on the second. Loosely following the [gamedev video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=il-TXbn5iMA), I implemented a `Brickmap` to compress the signed distance data. This typically compresses the data by a factor of 10-100, which can then be used for more quality. From that point on, I added another compressing procedure for colors and tried optimizing the initial SDF generation. Some stats for the example above: - 32 operations total, evaluated in an effective 512^3 grid in a -1..1 box - dense array: - 512^3 * 2 byte for each distance: 256MB - 512^3 * 3 byte RGB color: 384MB (not implemented) - total 640MB - time: 19.3s (unoptimized) - Brickmap: (memory rounded) - 1.5MB brick indices (73^3 * 4 byte) - ~~7.6MB~~ 10MB distances in bricks (~~14716~~ 14716/19683 bricks ¹, each 8^3 * 1 byte, depends on the amount of surface area) - 0.06MB index remapping for colors (~~14716~~ 14716/16384 * 4 byte indices ¹, one per brick) - 4.0MB color (~~2312~~ 2312/2744 bricks ¹, each 8^3 * 3 byte, depends on the number of mixed color bricks) - ¹ these are dynamically resizing arrays with n_used / n_available elements - total: ~~13.2MB~~ 15.5MB - time: ~~2.2s~~ ~~0.77s~~ ~~0.60s~~ 0.28s (with optimizations to skip empty regions and locally irrelevant SDF nodes) TODO: - [x] localized edits (don't regenerate everything on change, just what's needed) - [x] extend `ShaderAbstractions.Sampler` update functions https://github.com/SimonDanisch/ShaderAbstractions.jl/pull/31 - [x] allow prefix operations in merge nodes (union, diff, etc) - more Optimizations... - [ ] consider always adding position data to shapes to reduce number of translation operations (is this actually worth it, or do translation happen at other points to allow other operations to acts on the centered shape?) - [x] consider eliminating unneeded SDF nodes based on a SDF sample ~~rather than~~ and bounding boxes - [x] broadcast each sdf operation over a brick instead of broadcasting the tree as whole (i.e. evaluate `if command.id == ...` once per brick instead of once per brick element) - [ ] consider reusing brick indices for coarse distance sampling - [ ] 2D shapes for extrusion (etc) - [ ] maybe add rotational symmetry operation - [ ] improve user interface - [x] add methods for each shape and merge command in clean module/namespace - [ ] clean up old prototypes/unused code - [x] delete sdfplot, volume extension (use different parent plot instead) and related code - [x] consider replacing operation enum with Symbols - [ ] documentation - [ ] tests Note that this pr requires https://github.com/JuliaGeometry/GeometryBasics.jl/pull/276, https://github.com/SimonDanisch/ShaderAbstractions.jl/pull/31 I should also note that [Inigo Quilez articles](https://iquilezles.org/articles/) are very helpful for this pr, especially the one on 3D signed distance functions. Almost all the operations and shape functions come from there. ## Type of change - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) ## Checklist - [ ] Added an entry in CHANGELOG.md (for new features and breaking changes) - [ ] Added or changed relevant sections in the documentation - [ ] Added unit tests for new algorithms, conversion methods, etc. - [ ] Added reference image tests for new plotting functions, recipes, visual options, etc.
